is_anopheles.evidence: The paper mentions Anopheles species (An. stephensi, An. funestus, An. gambiae) in text references, but the experimental case study focuses exclusively on Aedes aegypti (page 1, 5).

reports_target_markers.evidence: No target resistance markers for Anopheles are genotyped. The study genotypes Vgsc mutations (V410L, V1016I, F1534C) in Aedes aegypti (page 4, Fig 3; page 5, Panel 2).

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: No extractable genotype counts or frequency data are reported for Anopheles populations.

african_field_population.evidence: The mosquito field samples analyzed in the case study were collected in Brazil (Americas). No African field populations of Anopheles were genotyped (page 4, Fig 3; page 5, Panel 2).

is_primary_study.evidence: This article is a Viewpoint / opinion paper discussing the policy and evolutionary impacts of domestic insecticide use, presenting a case study on Brazilian Aedes aegypti (page 1, 5).

sub_country_location.evidence: Mentions Campina Grande, João Pessoa, and Umbuzeiro in Paraíba State, Brazil (page 4, Fig 3a).

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: Mentions annual sampling/market data from 2011 to 2016 for the case study (page 4, Fig 3b).

duplicate_risk.evidence: Not applicable as the study is ineligible.

supplement.evidence: No supplementary file needed for this ineligible study.

assessment.summary: This viewpoint article discusses how the unregulated use of domestic (household) insecticides contributes to pyrethroid resistance in mosquito vectors. It presents a case study examining WHO tube/Peet Grady bioassays and Vgsc kdr mutations in Aedes aegypti from Brazil, but contains no genotype data for African Anopheles vectors.
exclusion_reasons: The paper is a Viewpoint article, not a primary field study of Anopheles vectors.
No target resistance markers listed in the protocol were genotyped in Anopheles.
The experimental case study focuses on Aedes aegypti from Brazil, not an African field population.
